items.name: Readability
items.evidence: In each select.types.ts, `import type { WindowSpec } from '~/sql/functions/window.ts';` sits in the middle of the file, after the type declarations. New imports were also put above the existing first import in the dialect files, and index.ts gained a stray blank line. Names are clear.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The window-name check (`if (!name || name.length === 0) throw ... non-empty`, plus the whitespace check) is copy-pasted into all five SelectQueryBuilderBase classes instead of one shared assert. The WINDOW chunk is also repeated in each dialect. The spec builder `renderWindowSpec` is shared.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Inputs are checked at the boundaries: preceding/following reject negative and non-integer values; ntile/nthValue reject non-positive values and the error includes the name and the value; rows/range check the boundary order; .window() rejects empty and whitespace-only names. Numbers go in via sql.raw, so none become bound parameters. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Public API additions are additive and consistent across dialects
items.name_zh: 公共 API 新增保持向后兼容且各方言一致
items.evidence: The change is purely additive. Each *SelectConfig gets an optional `windowList?` field, and pg, mysql, sqlite, gel and singlestore all get the same `.window(name, spec): this` method. The WINDOW chunk is undefined when no windows are set, so SQL for existing queries is unchanged. Exports go through sql/functions/index.ts.
